tools.name: browser_context
tools.description: Open or close a browser for this agent. "fresh" starts an empty throwaway profile with the legacy CLI, outside copied-profile protection. "mine" opens a private Edge/Chrome copy of the person's profile, without saved-login stores or linked files but with qualified cookie and encryption metadata; its snapshots and screenshots hide typed and editable values, and every command is yours to run, eval and run-code included. Both run in the background and leave the person's windows alone. A failed mine open never authorizes computer control, attaching to the person's browser, interactive sign-in, or switching identity or transport to get around it: COPY_SOURCE_PERMISSION means the OS refused access (Desk cannot grant it), COPY_SOURCE_POLICY means source qualification failed. The open reply carries runtime (Desk version and loaded plugin root), so a result binds to the code that produced it. Keep contextId and close when done; closing deletes the private folder, not screenshots in the evidence folder.

action.description: open starts a new browser and returns its contextId; close shuts it and deletes its folder.

browser.description: open only. fresh: initially empty legacy profile. mine: private copy of the person's profile that redacts typed values in what it reads, deleted on close. Defaults to fresh.

contextId.description: close only. The contextId that open returned.

tools.name: browser_command
tools.description: Run a command in an owned browser context. args is a list of literal strings, never shell. Start with ["goto","https://example.com"] or ["snapshot"], then act on current refs. In mine the commands are: snapshot [--interactive|--save], find <text>, goto <url>, go-back, go-forward, reload, wait [<seconds>|<text>|--gone <text>], click/dblclick/hover/check/uncheck <ref>, fill/type <ref> <text>, press [<ref>] <key>, select <ref> <value>, mousewheel <dx> <dy>, resize <w> <h>, screenshot [<ref>] [--full], tab-list, tab-new, tab-select <n>, tab-close [<n>], eval <function or expression> [<ref>], run-code <async function of page>, console [<level>], keydown/keyup <key>, mousemove <x> <y>, mousedown/mouseup [<button>], upload <ref> <file>..., dialog-accept [<text>], dialog-dismiss, localstorage-* and sessionstorage-* (list, get, set, delete, clear). All of them run as given; eval and run-code return what the script returns, unredacted, and a script's own error comes back as AUTH_SCRIPT_FAILED. A command mine does not have fails with AUTH_COMMAND_UNKNOWN and lists the ones it has. Every mine reply says where the tab is (page.url without query, page.title). An action says whether it navigated, changed the page in place (change, changeNote) or left it as your last read showed. A wait for text that has not shown stops early, saying why, once the page has been still for 10 seconds. A snapshot is compact, keeps controls and named lines on a long page, says how many lines it left out, and redacts typed and editable values; ["find","<text>"] shows just the lines holding that text with their refs. Act on a ref soon after its snapshot; on AUTH_SNAPSHOT_INVALIDATED snapshot again. To type into a rich-text editor, fill its textbox ref, then press Enter; typed.verified says whether it holds the text. screenshot saves a masked PNG in the evidence folder, which stays after close, and returns its path; [\"snapshot\",\"--save\"] writes a sanitized JSON artifact. Child frames show inside a frame node; framesOmitted counts any that could not be read. desk-web never opens desktop apps: when a page tries (msteams:, zoommtg:, slack:, mailto:), mine takes the page's own web path and says so in appLaunch. A transient error page: ["reload"], then wait. Closed shadow roots and refs whose element changed fail with a message saying what to do instead; an action may have applied before its post-action output failed. Fresh keeps the legacy CLI commands. Open and close only through browser_context.

contextId.description: The contextId that browser_context open returned.

args.description: The command and its arguments, for example ["snapshot"] or ["fill","e4","text"].
